pr.landing.title: Cinematic landing page
pr.landing.desc: Build a high-impact homepage with a clear story, strong art direction, and a focused call to action.
pr.landing.body: Act as a senior creative developer and UX strategist. Build a cinematic, responsive landing page for [BRAND], a [PRODUCT OR SERVICE] for [TARGET AUDIENCE]. Start by defining a clear visual concept, then implement the page in semantic HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Include a strong hero with one primary CTA, a concise value proposition, proof points, product benefits, and a final CTA. Use a coherent type scale, generous spacing, subtle motion, accessible contrast, responsive layouts, and reduced-motion support. Avoid generic filler, fake testimonials, dead links, and dependencies that are not necessary. Make every visible control work. Return the complete runnable code and briefly explain how to customize it.
pr.video.title: Video-first hero
pr.video.desc: Create a cinematic opening that still loads quickly and works when autoplay or video fails.
pr.video.body: Create a responsive, video-first hero for [BRAND]. Use a locally hosted or explicitly supplied video asset, a poster image fallback, muted inline playback, and a readable gradient overlay. Keep the headline and CTA in HTML rather than baked into the video. If the video fails or reduced motion is preferred, show the poster and keep all content visible. Lazy-load noncritical media, provide descriptive alt text for meaningful images, avoid layout shifts, and ensure controls remain keyboard accessible. Use subtle animation only where it supports the story. Return complete code plus an asset checklist; do not invent asset URLs.
pr.store.title: Storefront that sells
pr.store.desc: Design a product experience with honest cart behavior and a clear path to checkout.
pr.store.body: Build a responsive e-commerce storefront for [BRAND] selling [PRODUCT TYPE] to [AUDIENCE]. Include product cards with real supplied images and prices, search and category filters, variant selection where relevant, cart quantity controls, subtotal, and clear empty/loading/error states. Persist a demo cart only if useful, but label it as a prototype. Do not claim orders, payments, inventory, shipping, or authentication are real unless connected to a verified backend/provider. Separate UI from integration code and document what credentials, APIs, and server-side validation are needed for production. Include mobile and accessibility checks.
pr.audit.title: Conversion audit
pr.audit.desc: Find friction in the user journey and turn the findings into a prioritized improvement plan.
pr.audit.body: Audit this page as a senior conversion-focused product designer: [URL OR PAGE CODE]. First describe the intended audience and primary conversion goal. Then identify friction in the first screen, value proposition, hierarchy, trust signals, forms, mobile experience, performance, and CTA flow. For each issue, provide evidence from the supplied page, expected impact, effort, and a concrete fix. Prioritize the top five changes. Never invent analytics data or user research; label assumptions and propose experiments to validate them. Finish with revised headline and CTA copy options.
pr.system.title: Consistent design system
pr.system.desc: Turn scattered styles into reusable tokens and components without flattening the visual identity.
pr.system.body: Inspect the supplied website code and extract a lightweight design system. Define color tokens, typography roles, spacing scale, radii, shadows, breakpoints, focus states, and reusable button/card/form components. Preserve the existing brand identity and avoid unnecessary redesign. Replace duplicated values with CSS custom properties, consolidate repeated styles, and document component states including hover, focus, disabled, loading, and error. Check contrast and responsive behavior. Return the refactored code and a concise change summary; do not remove existing functionality.
pr.a11y.title: Accessibility pass
pr.a11y.desc: Improve keyboard use, semantics, contrast, and motion preferences with a focused checklist.
pr.a11y.body: Review the supplied website code for practical accessibility issues, aiming toward WCAG 2.2 AA. Check semantic landmarks, heading order, link and button names, keyboard navigation, visible focus, form labels and errors, dialog focus handling, color contrast, image alternatives, touch target sizes, and prefers-reduced-motion. Fix issues directly while preserving the visual design. Do not claim formal compliance without a full audit. Return the updated code and a short checklist of what changed and what still needs manual testing with keyboard and screen reader.
sp.title:
Not just one shark.
A whole ocean.
sp.intro: Explore a growing field guide of shark species. Search by name or habitat, filter the collection, and open a quick field note for each one.
sp.empty: No species match your search. Try another name or habitat.
sp.soon: Full species profiles with measurements and cited sources are coming soon.
sp.mako.name: Shortfin mako
sp.mako.desc: Built for speed, with a streamlined body and powerful tail.
sp.mako.fact: One of the fastest sharks, built for powerful bursts in open water. It is an active predator with a streamlined body and a pointed snout.
sp.white.name: Great white
sp.white.desc: A powerful hunter with a contrasting grey back and pale underside.
sp.white.fact: A large predatory shark found in cool and temperate seas. Its countershaded body helps it blend with the water when viewed from above or below.
sp.whale.name: Whale shark
sp.whale.desc: A gentle giant whose spotted pattern is unique to each individual.
sp.whale.fact: The largest living fish. Despite its size, it feeds mainly by filtering tiny organisms and small fish from the water.
sp.hammer.name: Scalloped hammerhead
sp.hammer.desc: Recognisable by its broad head and tendency to form schools.
sp.hammer.fact: Its wide, hammer-shaped head gives it a broad field of view and helps position sensory organs for detecting prey.
sp.tiger.name: Tiger shark
sp.tiger.desc: A versatile predator with faint tiger-like stripes along its body.
sp.tiger.fact: A large tropical and subtropical shark known for dark vertical markings, especially visible in younger individuals, and a broad diet.
sp.bull.name: Bull shark
sp.bull.desc: Stocky and adaptable, it can move between salt and fresh water.
sp.bull.fact: A robust coastal species that can tolerate both salt water and fresh water, allowing it to enter estuaries and some rivers.
sp.nurse.name: Nurse shark
sp.nurse.desc: A bottom-dweller often found resting around reefs and sandy flats.
sp.nurse.fact: A bottom-dwelling shark often resting on sandy seabeds or around reefs during the day, becoming more active at night.
sp.greenland.name: Greenland shark
sp.greenland.desc: A slow-moving deep-water species adapted to frigid northern seas.
sp.greenland.fact: A slow-moving shark of cold North Atlantic and Arctic waters, known for its exceptional longevity and deep-water lifestyle.
dv.title:
Built for speed,
tuned to strike once.
dv.intro: The shortfin mako is engineered end to end for fast, decisive movement. Your landing pages can work the same way: lean, quick, and focused.
dv.l1.p: Shark skin is covered in tiny tooth-like scales called dermal denticles. Their shape is thought to help reduce drag and keep water flowing smoothly along the body.
dv.l2.p: Sharks have electroreceptors called ampullae of Lorenzini that detect the faint electric fields of nearby animals, even prey hidden in sand.
dv.l3.p: Sharks continuously replace their teeth throughout life, with new rows ready behind the ones in use.
dv.l4.p: Makos rely on swimming to push water over their gills, so they keep moving to breathe. Forward motion is part of staying alive.

Make it bite.
